finding.claim: The ban endpoint swallows the authorization failure. require_admin() calls abort(403), which raises an HTTPException. The surrounding `except Exception` catches it and only logs a warning, so execution continues to do_ban(uid). Any authenticated non-admin user can ban arbitrary users.
finding.source: Any authenticated non-admin user sending POST /admin/users/<uid>/ban with an arbitrary uid
finding.sink: do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20, a privileged operation

trace.note: Route /admin/users/<uid>/ban is reachable with an attacker-chosen uid
For a non-admin, abort(403) is called, which raises werkzeug HTTPException (a subclass of Exception)
The handler only logs a warning and does not re-raise or return
do_ban(uid) runs unconditionally and returns ok=True

finding.guards_checked: require_admin does enforce the check, but its result is nullified by the broad except. There is no re-raise, no return in the handler and no other decorator or before_request hook in the file. The sibling unban route (admin.py:26) calls require_admin without try/except, so it is correctly protected. This is not a decoy.

verdict.guard_found: require_admin (admin.py:9-11) aborts with 403 for non-admins, but the call at admin.py:17 is wrapped in `except Exception` (admin.py:18) that only logs and falls through to do_ban. No re-raise, no return, no decorator, and no before_request hook in the file.
verdict.reason: At admin.py:17-20 the 403 HTTPException from abort(403) (admin.py:11) is caught by `except Exception` and only logged, so do_ban(uid) at admin.py:20 runs for any non-admin; the unban route at admin.py:26 has no try/except and is protected. One nit: the trace cites line 10 for abort(403), but the abort is on line 11 (line 10 is the `if`), which does not change the conclusion.
